title: Minimum Time to Revert Word to Initial State II
statement:
You get a string `word` and an integer `k`. Each second you must do two things, in this order: delete the first `k` characters of `word`, then append exactly `k` characters of your choice (any lowercase letters, not necessarily the deleted ones) to its end.

Return the smallest number of seconds, at least `1`, after which `word` can be equal to its original value again.
constraints: word contains only lowercase English letters
notes:
## Intuition

After `t` seconds the first `t * k` original characters are gone and the rest, `word.slice(t * k)`, now sits at the front; everything behind it was chosen freely. So the word can be restored exactly when that leftover suffix equals the prefix of the same length, or when `t * k >= n` and nothing original is left. Checking each suffix with a direct comparison costs O(n²/k) in the worst case. The Z-array answers every check in O(1): `z[i]` is the length of the longest common prefix of `word` and `word.slice(i)`, so the suffix at `i` is a prefix exactly when `z[i] === n - i`.

## Approach

1. Build `z` with the classic Z-algorithm, keeping the window `[left, right)` of the rightmost match found so far.
2. Inside that window, start `z[i]` from the mirrored value `z[i - left]` (capped at `right - i`), then extend it character by character.
3. Move the window whenever the match at `i` reaches past `right`.
4. Try `time = 1, 2, ...` while `time * k < n`: if `z[start] === n - start` for `start = time * k`, return `time`.
5. Otherwise the loop ends at the first `time` with `time * k >= n`; return it.

## Example 1, step by step

`word = "abacaba"`, `k = 3`. The Z-array is `[0, 0, 1, 0, 3, 0, 1]`. For `time = 1`, `start = 3` and `z[3] = 0`, but the suffix `"caba"` has length 4, so it fails. For `time = 2`, `start = 6` and `z[6] = 1 = 7 - 6`: the suffix `"a"` matches the prefix, so the answer is `2`.

## Complexity

- Time: O(n): the Z-algorithm moves `right` only forward, and the scan over `time` takes at most n / k steps.
- Space: O(n) for the Z-array.

## Pitfalls

- Comparing each surviving suffix with `startsWith` is fine for short words but O(n²/k) overall; with `k = 1` and n = 10^6 it is far too slow.
- Only shifts that are multiples of `k` matter; a matching suffix at another position is irrelevant.
- When `time * k >= n` every original character is gone, so that `time` always works; it is `ceil(n / k)`.

## Variables

| Name | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `n` | length of `word` |
| `z` | `z[i]` is the longest common prefix of `word` and its suffix at `i` |
| `left`, `right` | the rightmost match window `[left, right)` found so far |
| `time` | number of seconds being tested |
| `start` | where the surviving original suffix begins after `time` seconds |
